label: Aquinas, I q.6 a.1 co.: God as first efficient cause is desirable through his effects
interpretation: An effect's perfection bears a likeness to the agent, so what is desirable in the agent is the participation of that likeness. The second reply allows a natural appetite without cognition, alongside sensible and rational cases.
attribution: The passage states that goodness belongs preeminently to God as first efficient cause: effects seek their own perfections, and in doing so desire a likeness of their cause, which is the premise.
